text: Let $G_n$ be the partition graph on the partitions associated with the parameter $n$, and consider its simplicial thick zones, including the tetrahedral and higher-order regions. The front extremes and antennas refer to the frontal extremal parts of the graph, while the rear-central part and central rear body refer to the corresponding geometric regions described by the shell/core structure. **Rear-central nucleation conjecture.** For all sufficiently large $n$, the first genuinely higher simplicial behaviour of the partition graph is nucleated in the rear-central part of $G_n$. Equivalently, the earliest tetrahedral and higher-order thick zones are asymptotically separated from the front extremes and are organized around the central rear body of the graph rather than around its antennas. This strengthens the observed fact that substantial thickening begins in a rear-central region rather than at the front. Computational examples suggest a relationship with the self-conjugate axis and the spine, but the claim does not assert that maximal-thickness vertices lie on the axis, remain at bounded distance from the spine, or that higher-dimensional thick regions are connected or unique.

The self-conjugate consecutive-core and symmetric generalized Dyck path conjecture
https://mathdb.com/p/342347/the-self-conjugate-consecutive-core-and-symmetric-generalize

Let $s$ and $k$ be positive integers. A **self-conjugate $(s,s+1,\dots,s+k)$-core** is a self-conjugate partition that is simultaneously an $s$-core, $(s+1)$-core, and so on through an $(s+k)$-core. A **symmetric $(s,k)$-generalized Dyck path** is a generalized Dyck path with parameters $(s,k)$ that is invariant under the relevant reflection symmetry. **Self-conjugate consecutive-core conjecture.** The number of self-conjugate $(s,s+1,\dots,s+k)$-cores is equal to the number of symmetric $(s,k)$-generalized Dyck paths. This extends the proved case of three consecutive core parameters established earlier in the paper; the conjecture proposes the corresponding equality for every pair of positive integers $s$ and $k$.

https://mathdb.com/p/327855/armstrong-hanusa-jones-average-size-conjecture-for-core-part

A partition is an **$(s,t)$-core** if it is simultaneously an $s$-core and a $t$-core, and it is **self-conjugate** if its Ferrers diagram is invariant under conjugation. For coprime positive integers $s$ and $t$, consider the finite sets of $(s,t)$-core partitions and self-conjugate $(s,t)$-core partitions, with size given by the number of cells in the Ferrers diagram.

**Armstrong–Hanusa–Jones conjecture.** The average size in each of these two sets is

$$
\frac{(s+t+1)(s-1)(t-1)}{24}.
$$

The conjecture concerns a common statistic on two related finite families of core partitions. The paper states that the self-conjugate case is proved using a bijection with lattice paths; the source therefore treats this conjecture as resolved.

Uniform interpolation-error conjecture for self-conjugate grids

Let $I$ be the interpolation interval, let $\mathbb{D}$ be the unit disc, let $\mathscr{E}_n(\mathbb{D})$ be the entire functions $g:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ satisfying $\|g^{(n)}\|_{\mathbb{D}}\leqslant1$, and let $z_{1:n}\in\mathbb{D}^n$ be a self-conjugate grid. Let $f(\cdot\mid z_{1:n})$ be the nodal polynomial and $\hat g(\cdot\mid z_{1:n})$ the interpolation polynomial.

**Self-conjugate-grid uniform conjecture.** For every $0\leqslant k\leqslant n-1$,

$$
\operatorname{\mathsf{sup}}_{g\in\mathscr{E}_n(\mathbb{D})}\|g^{(k)}(\cdot)-\hat g^{(k)}(\cdot\mid z_{1:n})\|_I=\frac{1}{n!}\|f^{(k)}(\cdot\mid z_{1:n})\|_I.
$$

Equivalently, the source gives the corresponding supremum identity involving Schur polynomials. This would generalize the real-node result of Kallioniemi and Shadrin to self-conjugate grids in the unit disc; the source does not provide a resolution.

ikely that the structure identified by Kallioniemi and Shadrin in the real setup is preserved – in other words, this set consists of nonoverlapping segments, and z\mapsto|[g(z)-\hat{g}(z|z_{1:n})]^{\vskip-2.84544pt(k)}| is maximized at an endpoint of each complementary segment. This would imply that Shadrin’s result generalizes to self-conjugate grids in {\mathbb{D}}^{n} , prompting the following Conjecture 6.3. For any 0\leqslant k\leqslant n-1 and arbitrary self-conjugate grid z_{1:n}\in{\mathbb{D}}^{n} , it holds that (36) \sup_{g\in\mathscr{E}_{n}({\mathbb{D}})}\|g^{(k)}(\cdot)-\hat{g}^{(k)}(\cdot|z_{1:n})\|_{I}=\frac{1}{n!}\|f^{(k)}(\cdot|z_{1:n})\|_{I}\,, or equivalently in terms of Schur polynomials: \sup_{t\in{\mathbb{N}}_{n}}\left\{{\binom{t}{n}}^{-1}\max_{z\in I}\left|\sum_{d=0}^{t-n}{\binom{t}{n+d}}z^{t-n-d}\mathsf{s}_{(d|n-k-1)}(z_{1:n}-z1_{n})\right|\right\}=\max_{z\in I}|\mathsf{e}_{n-k}(z_{1:n}-z1_{n})|\,. Here, one must study the sum in the left-hand side analytically as a polynomial in z\in I , possibly using the result of Weigandt [38, 39] that expresses \sum_{j\in[n]}\frac{\partial}{\partial x_{j}}\mathsf{s}_{\lambda}(x_{1:n}) in terms of Schur polynomials. Palindromic case. We now briefly discuss the case z_{1:n}\in{\mathbb{T}}^{n} . Since \bar{z}=1/z on {\mathbb{T}} , polynomial f(z) coincides with its reciprocal z^{n}f(1/z) , i.e. is palindromic: f_{k}=f_{n-k} for 0\leqslant k\leqslant n . Equivalently, the dynamical system defined in (1) is time-reversible. Of possible relevance here is the result in [40], recasting \mathsf{s}_{\lambda}(x_{1},\dots,x_{n},1/x_{1},\dots,1/x_{n}) as a Schur polynomial in the variables x_{j}+1/x_{j} . Invoking we see that \operatorname{\mathsf{Im}}(z_{1:n}) vanish here, along with the difficulties they used to cause. On the flip side, the new parametrization might complicate the nice algebraic structure associated with hook partitions. 6.3. Reduction to monomials. We now reduce the suprema over \mathscr{E}_{n}({\mathbb{D}}) in (35)–(36) to those over monomials. Interchanging \sup_{g\in\mathscr{E}_{n}({\mathbb{D}})} and \sup_{z\in I} in (36), it suffices to treat the pointwise case. Proposition 6.2. For z\in\mathbb{C} and simple z_{1:n}\in\mathbb{C}^{n}, the functional g\in\mathscr{E}_{n}({\mathbb{D}})\mapsto|[g(z)-\hat{g}(z|z_{1:n})]{}^{(k)}| is maximized on a monomial of the form \frac{(m-n)!}{m!}z^{m} , m\geqslant n . Proof. For any z\in\mathbb{C} and simple z_{1:n}\in\mathbb{C}^{n} , the above functional is convex and continuous on \mathscr{E}_{n}({\mathbb{D}}) (with respect to the uniform metric on {\mathbb{D}} ). Now, let \mathscr{H}_{n}({\mathbb{D}}) be the set of functions holomorphic on {\mathbb{D}} with \|g^{(n)}\|_{\mathbb{D}}\leqslant 1 . By Montel’s theorem, \mathscr{H}_{n}({\mathbb{D}}) is precompact; hence \mathscr{E}_{n}({\mathbb{D}}) is compact as its closed subset. By the Krein-Milman theorem and Bauer’s maximum principle, it suffices to show that all extreme points of \mathscr{E}_{n}({\mathbb{D}}) are of the form \frac{(m-n)!}{m!}az^{m}+p(z) , where a\in{\mathbb{T}} and p(z) is a polynomial of degree less than n . Considering [\cdot]^{(k)} as a linear operator, we reduce arbitrary n\in{\mathbb{N}}_{0} to n=0 , in which case the claim follows from Lemma 6.1 below. \square Lemma 6.1. Extreme points of the set of entire functions with modulus \leqslant 1 on {\mathbb{T}} are monomials. Proof. To be an extreme point of \mathscr{E}_{0}({\mathbb{D}}) , g has to satisfy \|g\|_{{\mathbb{D}}}=1 , i.e. have a nonempty support set \mathsf{Supp}(g):=\{z\in{\mathbb{T}}:|g(z)|=1\}. A classical result (e.g. [41, II.I.3]) is that for any entire function g , \mathsf{Supp}(g) is either the whole {\mathbb{T}} or a finite set. In the former case, g must be a monomial. Indeed, g_{0}(z):=1/\overline{g(1/\overline{z})} is meromorphic on \mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\} and coincides with g

Positivity conjecture for self-conjugate 6-core partitions

Let $sc_6(n)$ denote the number of self-conjugate $6$-core partitions of $n$, and let $n$ be a positive integer. **Positivity conjecture for self-conjugate 6-core partitions.**

$$
sc_6(n)>0
$$

except when $n\in\{2,12,13,73\}$. The claim is based on computed values through $n=10000$; the source gives no proof of the complete characterization.

Let $A_n$ be the alternating group, and let $p$ and $q$ be odd primes satisfying

$$
9<p,q<n-17.
$$

**Defect-zero block monotonicity conjecture.** The number of defect zero $p$-blocks of $A_n$ is strictly less than the number of defect zero $q$-blocks of $A_n$. This conjecture is motivated by experimental inequalities for non-self-conjugate core partitions; the source gives no proof.
